study.question: Can a context-shared sparse first buy affine preserve112 nonlinear channels and the current best click AUC while reducing measured prediction cost, and does separating target from corrected history outperform an equally sparse mixed grouping and nearly parameter-matched dense narrowing?
study.hypothesis: Observation: dense112/64 reference reaches click AUC0.6671669182126774; width96 falls to0.6669282617886453; width108 to0.666627507052977; second48 to0.6662416907813548. Alternative96-channel subsets and rank73 factors also lose AUC. Rank73 balanced/output-heavy yield0.6668143579868517/0.6668091428093557 with p50 latency15.1982/15.1328ms versus reference15.1243ms, so low-rank utility is unsupported. These do not establish that every input-to-channel connection is needed. Hypothesis: preserving nonlinear breadth but postponing direct target/history mixing to the second dense layer may retain the buy context-learning signal with fewer first-layer connections. Both branches retain all context coordinates. The buy residual is already a full-input joint function, so the intervention reduces direct first-affine connectivity, not all cross-source information. This is an unverified local hypothesis; rank/channel failures do not refute it and no novelty claim is made.

Here no new tokens or mixer are used: only one existing buy affine gets shared-context two-branch sparsity. Benchmark source is primary evidence of that reimplementation, not proof of original-paper equivalence.

study.proposed_difference: After all inherited construction, resets, slicing and scale controls finish, replace only buy first affine W[112,400] by two56-row trainable packed affines. Both read all192 context coordinates; semantic branch0 also reads target96, branch1 corrected pooled history112. Thus stored weights are56x288+56x304 instead of112x400, biases remain112 and all later state remains intact. Each packed coefficient clones its exact source row/column with no new RNG, normalization or rescaling. Both partitions use fixed registered integer gather buffers, two F.linear calls and concatenation in both train and eval; no full weight reconstruction, cache, dynamic routing or sparse-masked dense Parameters. The mixed replacement has identical branch sizes but allocates half of each target field and half of each corresponding pooled field to branch0; action and complements go to branch1. Dense width87/64 is matched within2 trainable parameters. The grouping does not remove any supplied feature from the model.
predictions: Freeze before execution: same-seed screening AUC preservation means candidate minus concurrent dense bridge >=-0.0001000, AND candidate absolute AUC>=0.6670669182126774 based on current best. Original frozen entry0.666753547526167 and DIN0.6555440824200336 remain utility references, not a weaker selection threshold. Bridge disagreement exceeding1e-6 AUC or parameter mismatch blocks comparison until explained; diagnostic/retry costs remain charged.

Analytic expected dense counts: dense reference204531, dense width87192881, semantic/mixed192883; all embedding counts31793216. Partition saves11648 dense parameters (5.695%) but only0.0364% of total. Host must measure counts, memory and compute; do not present dense saving as total-model saving.

For preliminary utility require AUC preservation plus at least1% lower model-only batch latency p50 and p95 versus concurrent bridge, under the unchanged host evaluator. Full-validation inference seconds and throughput, train/wall seconds, peak memory, examples processed and all four AUC/Logloss are reported separately. A single noisy timing win remains provisional. Repeated timing at same batch/machine/precision and alternating order, if authorized later, must confirm median p50 and p95 ratios<=0.99; total inference seconds must not regress by more than1%. Training-time ratio>1.05 rejects training-efficiency utility even if prediction utility remains supported.

Conditional allocation prediction: semantic achieves greater click AUC than dense87 at near-identical parameter budget; semantic also exceeds the equal-sparsity mixed replacement if modality-aligned first-layer allocation matters. A positive screening contrast must be repeated before attributing mechanism. Report each delta; the mixed control can support breadth/sparsity utility without supporting semantic grouping.

Report all four tasks separately and auxiliary mean apart from click selection. Existing private-head reductions severely degrade auxiliary quality versus DIN; click-preserving sparsity must not be described as preserving joint four-task quality. Use inherited history-length slices with sample/positive/negative counts; all other posthoc slices exploratory.
falsifiers: Either partition losing more than0.0001 click AUC against the reproduced current-best bridge rejects its prescribed preservation utility in this run, even if it beats original entry or DIN.
No measured inference cost reduction, or a cost increase from index_select, allocations or extra GEMM launches, rejects prediction-efficiency utility despite lower parameter/MAC counts.
Semantic no better than mixed under repeated controlled comparisons does not support modality alignment; both failing while dense87 succeeds rejects this partition allocation.
A win of semantic versus dense87 alone cannot establish breadth as the cause: initialization, representational topology, parameter geometry and global dense gradient clipping remain alternatives.

Bridge mismatch, wrong retained storage/parameter ownership, missing gradients or changed masks invalidates the contrast rather than constituting scientific counterevidence. Retain failed receipts and costs. One failed partition does not establish all full-input connectivity necessary.
alternative_explanations: Single-seed variance, repeated validation adaptation/selection bias and runtime drift; no holdout feedback is available
Changed inherited-template fan-in lowers initial preactivation variance; semantic/mixed have matching branch fan-in and row allocation but different input distributions
Packed branches alter optimizer parameter grouping and floating-point accumulation; global dense gradient clipping can couple private losses back to click updates
Buy residual already mixes full inputs; retained cross-source information there may compensate, so mechanism is limited to direct first-affine connectivity
Dense87 and sparse112 differ nonlinear width, Dice state and topology in addition to allocation; two-parameter mismatch is negligible but explicitly reported
Extra gather memory traffic/kernel launches can dominate small saved MACs; predictions remain unmeasured
Mixed replacement is one fixed coordinate split with asymmetric pooled action access; it is neither a random-sparsity average nor a complete test of semantic partitions
